title: tokens-qps-headroom-sensitivity-by-gpu-family-2027q2
description: Working spreadsheet: sensitivity calc for tokens/sec headroom and reserve GPU targets by region and GPU family. Emphasis on multi-region resilience buffer and how different GPU families shift reserve needs for hosted API peak windows.
summary: This sheet estimates capacity vs expected peak tokens/sec for four representative regions, broken out by GPU family and model profile. We run a 95th percentile peak scenario and compute headroom and a recommended reserve GPU count to hit our resilience target (failover + 20% buffer). The doc includes quick sensitivity runs for -20% and +20% effective tokens/sec per GPU to capture kernel/runtime/quantization variance.
assumptions: avg_tokens_per_request = 75 tokens (used only for QPS conversions elsewhere)
tokens_per_gpu_est are runtime-effective numbers (account for batching, kv-cache reuse, mixed-precision). These are conservative engineering estimates, not peak theoretical FLOPS.
peak_tokens_sec_95p is the expected 95th percentile sustained tokens/sec during a peak window (not instantaneous burst).
recommended_reserve_gpus = ceil(headroom_tokens_sec / tokens_per_gpu_est). Reserve is rounded up and should be held cold-warm depending on contract type.
target resilience policy: tolerate one major-region outage + 20% headroom on surviving regions (this sheet builds per-region reserve, ops to centralize runbook still required).
sensitivity_scenarios: -20% effective tokens_per_gpu: increases reserve needs by ~25-30% across H100/A100/L40s due to rounding and distribution of load.
+20% effective tokens_per_gpu: reduces reserve GPUs materially for 13B/7B profiles; 70B remains dominated by KV/cache characteristics so gains are smaller.

region-outage scenario: compute deficit = affected_region_peak_tokens_sec * failover_fraction_assumed. For full failover (100%) surviving regions would require aggregated reserve GPUs = sum(deficit / tokens_per_gpu across survivors).
quick_interpretation: If we provision per the recommended_reserve_gpus above and keep autoscale headroom configured, we hit our resilience mandate for single-region failures for typical model mixes. H100-heavy regions (us-west1, us-east4) show larger absolute reserve counts because effective tokens/sec per GPU varies heavily by model size (70B much lower).
recommended_actions: Prioritize a 'cold pool' of reserved GPUs in europe-west1 (A100) sized ~120 GPUs that can be spun to warm in 15-30m as a low-cost buffer for cross-region failover.

Add runtime telemetry flags to measure effective tokens/sec per GPU over the next 4 weeks, segmented by model_profile and request-length buckets; feed measurements back into tokens_per_gpu_est and re-run this sheet bi-weekly.
Implement a canary routing rule to limit cross-region failover QPS to 60% of normal per-second load until we've validated KV cache warmup behavior under failover.
Evaluate negotiated burst capacity with cloud partners for up to 10% of peak tokens/sec as a short-term mitigation while reserve pools are being built.
Track reserve cost delta in cost center INFRA-RESERVE and submit monthly decking to finance for committed capacity decisions.
notes_and_open_questions: Need confirmation from runtime team on tokens_per_gpu_est methodology; current values use simplified kernel/policy multipliers.
If average request length shifts to 120 tokens, QPS conversions change materially — product should provide 90-day request-length histogram.
Consider model pinning for critical customers during outage windows to avoid 70B cold-start amplification.
Should we maintain region-specific cold pools (recommended) vs a single global pool? Ops cost vs failover latency tradeoffs need decision.
